attribution.note: Marcus's own closing words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: 'Not one law has passed' is normalised as 'no federal AI law'. In context Marcus means laws protecting against the listed harms (disinformation, deepfakes, cybercrime), so the normalisation widens the scope to any AI-related statute ever enacted.

contract.note: The plain reading counts any federal AI-related law with an open start date, including a 2020 NSF research act. In context an informed reader takes 'not one law' to mean no protective AI legislation. The broad reading is stretched against the speaker, and the contract admits the narrower reading changes the result.

evidence.note: IOGAN Act (Dec 2020) directs research on deepfake detection. It is a genuine enactment but not a protective law against the harms Marcus lists, so on a fair reading it does not contradict him.
FCC finding documents AI-cloned Biden robocalls aimed at deterring New Hampshire primary voters in Jan 2024. Supports the elections component. Published Sept 2024, before the cutoff.
FBI warning from June 2023 on deepfake sextortion. Too early and unquantified to establish prevalence at April 2024.

reviews.rationale: The elections component is supported by e3. 'Thrall' has no testable threshold, and the packet does not establish how widespread deepfake scams were at publication. The contract's broad legislative reading, contradicted only by a 2020 research act, is not a fair ordinary reading. On the fair reading (protective law), the packet holds no complete legislative record. The claim cannot be settled.
